SUPERSEDED.further_caveat: even the FP8 reference cannot validate this fixture's expert region: an independent dequantisation puts the expert projection at absmax 119.3 against a swiglu_limit of 10, so 99.8%-100% of routed values saturate the clamp. results/abi3/deepseek_v41_reduced_fixture_saturates.json records that, and build/models/deepseek-v4.1-flash-reduced-v2 is the fixture built to fix it (expert E8M0 exponent -5, weights absmax 0.1875).
two_independent_reasons: its routed experts are DEAD: it ran the vendor's FP4 expert kernel, which on this machine returns exactly zero for every routed expert's second projection (11 of 11 measured), so its token came from a shared-expert-only model. See deepseek_v41_reduced_oracle_dead_experts.json

its provenance is stale: it records checkpoint lock c38e77599e941b07 over 3 verified files, while the committed lock results/abi3/deepseek_v41_reduced_checkpoint.lock.json is 2c63f413e81951ab over 5. The lock has not been modified since commit bb5a580; this artifact predates it.

architecture_under_test.why: the CSA2 mode sequence and every arity are the released model's; only magnitudes are reduced, which is what makes a G1f run a witness about this architecture

fixture_record_agreement.why: the fixture builder generated from weights held in memory; this run generated from the bytes it wrote. Agreement is what makes the fixture reproducible

reference_implementation.loader: the release's own inference/model.py Transformer, built from the fixture's inference_config.json and loaded from its shard
reference_implementation.why_no_cross_check: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has no transformers modelling code, so there is no second greedy implementation to compare against; the Qwen predecessor cross-checks against transformers.generate and this one cannot. What IS cross-checked is the fixture record: the same ids from weights in memory and from the bytes on disk

weight_loading.dequantization: attn.wo_a ships fp8 with a 32x32-blocked E8M0 scale, as the released checkpoint's own shard header does, and is dequantized to bf16 here -- the release's convert.py step, which its model.py names beside the einsum that consumes the weight. This one IS a conversion and not a reinterpretation, and it is lossy in the same way the release's is
weight_loading.reinterpretation: packed FP4 expert weights are stored as I8, the released checkpoint's own convention, and restored to float4_e2m1fn_x2 by viewing the same bytes
weight_loading.widening: the checkpoint stores head.weight, the compressor's projections and the MTP heads in BF16 where the vendor module holds F32, as the released checkpoint's own shard headers do. Widening is exact; the bits the narrowing dropped are absent from the fixture's own generation too
